_comment: P13-E03-T10. A live probe on 2026-09-05 found chatislam.org serving NO
Content-Security-Policy on ordinary pages -- so the only clickjacking
control was X-Frame-Options: SAMEORIGIN above, and frame-ancestors, the
modern control the org's own security-headers SOT calls 'primary', was
absent. The edge Transform Rules that were supposed to supply it are in
effect on none of the eight zones, so the origin is the only layer we
actually control.
WHY THIS IS NOT SIMPLY ADDED TO THE /(.*) RULE ABOVE:
the /widget(.*) rule below deliberately allows framing by ummat.app. When
two CSP headers both apply, browsers INTERSECT them -- and
'none' intersected with https://ummat.app is nothing. Putting
frame-ancestors 'none' on the catch-all would therefore silently kill the
widget's embed policy. The negative lookahead keeps /widget* on exactly
the behaviour it has today.
The source pattern was verified locally against path-to-regexp 6.3.0
before being committed: it matches /, /about, /chat, /api/health and
/api/widget/send, and does NOT match /widget, /widget/embed.js or
/widget/foo/bar.
Two observations recorded but deliberately NOT acted on here, because
each needs its own verification rather than a drive-by edit:
1. /widget(.*) is ALSO permanently redirected to /chat further down
this file, so no widget document is currently served at all and that
header block may be vestigial. Left alone -- if the redirect is ever
removed the embed policy must still be correct.
2. X-Frame-Options: ALLOW-FROM (in that block) is obsolete and honoured
by no current browser; the widget's protection rests entirely on its
CSP frame-ancestors, which is correct and present.
